title: Toolchain invocation ergonomics: async hydration, parallel backoff, and structured result merging
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Improves tool-calling ergonomics: introduces async result hydration for multi-tool graphs, deterministic merge strategy for structured outputs, and exponential backoff/retry plumbing for parallel tool invocations. Backward-compatible with existing OpenAI-style function-calling semantics.
description: Motivation: Customers are using multi-tool call graphs (chain-of-tools + parallel tool fans) and need safer, more ergonomic ways to hydrate tool outputs back into downstream tool inputs while preserving deterministic structured output shapes. This PR adds an async hydration layer on the tool invocation path, a deterministic merging strategy for structured results (JSON schema merging + conflict resolution policy), and robust retry/backoff semantics for tools invoked in parallel. Goals: 1) Make multi-tool flows less error-prone for app developers; 2) Reduce silent races when parallel tool calls return at different times; 3) Keep OpenAI-compatibility for function/tool calling while exposing more explicit ergonomics for engineering teams.

notes: Implementation details: the async hydration layer attaches a hydration token to each tool invocation; results are streamed back into a per-request ledger, which the merger consumes when either all expected results arrive or a soft timeout triggers. Retry semantics: parallel fanouts use exponential backoff with jitter and a shared circuit-breaker per tool type to avoid thundering herds. OpenAI compatibility: preserved function-calling signature; hydrateToolResults returns outputs in both OpenAI-style 'arguments' and Redwood's structured result wrapper. Backwards compatibility: default merge policy is 'prefer-schema' which preserves stable behavior for existing customers while surfacing conflicts to the application via telemetry and structured error payloads.
benchmark_notes: Microbenchmarks (local perf lab): multi-tool fanout with 8 parallel tools: 0.5% throughput regression, p95 latency change < 2ms; failure scenarios show 30-45% fewer application-level reconciliation errors. Canary telemetry shows a modest 2% increase in control-plane calls due to hydration bookkeeping, acceptable vs. reliability gains.
migration_guide: For most customers: no action required. To opt into experimental stricter merging, set config 'tool.merge.policy=strict-error' in console or private config. SDKs: new helper hydrateToolResults() available in TS SDK; Python SDK shim to follow in subsequent PR. Note: if you rely on non-deterministic merge behavior, test with the new harness first.
